# DietView

> Interactive, hierarchical visualization of predator diet data

Stomach contents are identified to uneven depth: one prey is named to
species, the next only to “Teleostei”, and some material cannot be
placed at all. DietView keeps all of it. From a long table with one row
per prey record, it attaches a taxonomic lineage (from WoRMS, the GBIF
Backbone, or a lineage table you supply), keeps every record that
stopped at a coarse rank as an explicit *unidentified* category below
that rank, and shows the whole diet at every rank in one sunburst, by
prey records or by weight. It also reports the classical frequency of
occurrence, how identification depth changes with digestion, and can
write the result to a single HTML file that opens in any browser. The
same tools work beyond stomachs: DNA metabarcoding of scats or gut
contents (sequence reads summarized as relative read abundance),
pellets, regurgitates, and other compositional data such as catch or
benthic samples. See the [documentation
site](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/).

## Overview

DietView is built around a single input contract (*one row per prey
record in a sampling unit*, usually a stomach) and one reusable
specification object. From there it offers:

- **taxonomy on demand**: resolve prey against WoRMS by AphiaID
  (preferred) or name, following unaccepted names to their valid
  AphiaID, with exact matching first, then WoRMS TAXAMATCH for
  misspellings, and a provenance log to review; resolve terrestrial and
  freshwater prey against the GBIF Backbone with the same rules; or join
  a lineage table for a fully offline, reproducible run;
- **within-rank importance** in two currencies (prey records and
  weight), where every taxonomic rank sums to 100 % and unidentified
  prey is an explicit **NA** category rather than a dropped row;
- **covariate stratification** by any user-declared columns (period,
  year, size class, length bins, region, …), plus helpers to derive
  periods and length bins;
- an **identification-resolution diagnostic**: the finest rank each
  record reaches, by predator, method or any covariate, and by digestion
  stage, to show how identification degrades with digestion;
- **other data shapes**: wide sample-by-taxon tables (ASV/OTU tables,
  catch compositions) and pipeline lineage strings (QIIME 2, SILVA,
  MIDORI, BOLD) come in with
  [`dv_from_wide()`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/dv_from_wide.md)
  and
  [`dv_parse_lineage()`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/dv_parse_lineage.md);
  sequence reads are declared as such and summarized as relative read
  abundance (RRA);
- **interactive sunbursts** (plotly), with one color per taxon kept the
  same in every panel, so strata can be compared at a glance;
- three **outputs**: a [Shiny](https://shiny.posit.co/) explorer, a
  self-contained HTML dashboard (searchable, sortable predator cards,
  with optional ID photos from iNaturalist or Wikimedia Commons, each
  credited with its author and license), or plain plotly figures;
- **exploration & reproducible aggregation**: sample summaries,
  prey-accumulation curves for sampling sufficiency, classical per-rank
  frequency of occurrence, threshold-based aggregation that collapses
  rare prey upward to a reproducible resolution (pooled, cross-predator,
  and per-predator), and a sampling-unit by prey-category matrix export
  for multivariate analysis.

The package ships real, public data to learn on: `ices_diet` (9,639 prey
records from 4,231 stomachs of 22 fish species, North Sea,
Skagerrak-Kattegat and Baltic Sea, 2020-2024), `ices_stomachs` (every
sampled stomach, empty ones included) and `ices_lineage` (their frozen
WoRMS classification). Source: ICES Stomach Content Database, ICES,
Copenhagen; extract distributed with the R package stomachr (Lindmark
2026). See
[`?ices_diet`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/ices_diet.md).
For DNA-based diet, it also ships `salish_seal_dna`, the metabarcoding
diet of 4,625 harbour seal scats from the Salish Sea (Thomas et
al. 2022, *Scientific Data*, CC0), with its frozen WoRMS lineage
`salish_seal_lineage`.

## Installation

Install DietView from GitHub:

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("SostheneA/DietView")
```

Optional features need a few more packages: `worrms` (WoRMS taxonomy)
and `shiny` + `DT` (interactive app). GBIF taxonomy needs no extra
package, only internet access. The HTML dashboard needs neither
`rmarkdown` nor pandoc.

``` r

install.packages(c("worrms", "shiny", "DT"))
```

## Basic use

A minimal, fully offline workflow on the bundled ICES stomach data (a
long table of prey records plus a frozen lineage lookup, so no internet
is required):

``` r

library(DietView)

# 1. base long table: one row per prey record, NO taxonomy columns
#    (drop non-food items and nematodes, which are mostly parasites, not prey)
phylum <- ices_lineage$phylum[match(ices_diet$prey_aphia_id, ices_lineage$prey_aphia_id)]
dat <- ices_diet[ices_diet$item_type != "non_food" & !phylum %in% "Nematoda", ]

# 2. declare column roles once (nothing is hard-coded)
spec <- dv_spec(
  predator       = "predator_common",
  predator_latin = "predator_latin",
  stomach        = "stomach_id",
  prey_id        = "prey_aphia_id",
  prey_name      = "prey_name",
  weight         = "prey_weight_g",
  count          = "prey_count",
  digestion      = "digestion_label",
  covariates     = c("region", "year", "quarter")
)

# 3. attach taxonomy -- offline via a lineage table ...
prep <- dv_prepare(dat, spec, taxonomy = "table", lineage = ices_lineage,
                   verbose = FALSE)

#    ... or live from WoRMS (needs 'worrms' + internet; results are cached):
# prep <- dv_prepare(dat, spec, taxonomy = "worms")

# 4. metrics: within-rank importance (NA included; each rank sums to 100 %)
tree <- dv_tree(prep)
dv_rank_table(tree, "Class")

# 5. figures + digestion diagnostic, here for Atlantic cod
cod <- dv_prepare(dat[dat$predator_common == "Atlantic cod", ], spec,
                  taxonomy = "table", lineage = ices_lineage, verbose = FALSE)
dv_sunburst(dv_tree(cod), mode = "occurrence", title = "Atlantic cod")
dv_digestion_diagnostic(cod, by = "region")

# 6. explore, check sampling sufficiency, aggregate, and export
dv_summary(prep)                                  # stomachs, records, taxa per predator
dv_prey_accumulation(cod, permutations = 50, seed = 1)  # cumulative prey curve
dv_fo_table(cod, rank = "class")                  # classical per-rank %FO

agg  <- dv_aggregate_threshold(cod, threshold = 10)    # prey in < 10 stomachs move up a rank
m    <- dv_matrix(agg, currency = "occurrence")        # set x category matrix (-> vegan)

# 7. write a standalone HTML dashboard (one file, opens in any browser)
dv_deploy(cod, file = "cod_dashboard.html", dir = tempdir(),
          strata = c("region", "quarter"),
          length_col = "length_cm")

# or explore interactively
run_dietview(prep)
```

See [Getting started with
DietView](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/articles/getting-started.html)
for the rendered walk-through.

## The explicit-NA philosophy

Where identification stops, or WoRMS has no finer rank, DietView keeps
the deeper rank columns as `NA` and shows them as an explicit **“NA”**
category (white in the sunburst). Two consequences follow:

- within-rank percentages still sum to **100 %**, so nothing is quietly
  rebased onto the identified fraction only;
- identification gaps stay **visible** instead of being hidden inside a
  functional grouping.

The digestion diagnostic makes this concrete. On real surveys, records
identified to species become rarer as digestion advances, and more of
them stop at a coarse rank or stay unresolved; the diagnostic shows by
how much, instead of hiding it.

## Input format

One row = **one prey record in one stomach**. Column names are free; you
map them to DietView roles once via
[`dv_spec()`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/dv_spec.md).
The bundled `ices_diet` table is in this format: one row per prey
record, with the stomach-level variables (predator, length, haul,
region, year, …) repeated on each row, and its lineage lookup is
`ices_lineage` (ICES Stomach Content Database, ICES, Copenhagen; extract
distributed with the R package stomachr, Lindmark 2026; see
[`?ices_diet`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/ices_diet.md)).
The data dictionary (`inst/extdata/dietview_data_dictionary.md`) also
documents the small 24-record example `dietview_example.csv` (base
table) and `dietview_example_lineage.csv` (lineage lookup), kept for
tests and quick checks of the mechanics.

## Beyond stomach contents

The input contract is not tied to stomachs: any table of taxa with a
quantity, inside sampling units, with covariates, fits. Declare what the
quantity is and what a unit is, and every figure, table and dashboard
follows:

``` r

# DNA metabarcoding of harbour seal scats (bundled, CC0)
spec <- dv_spec(predator = "predator", stomach = "sample_id",
                prey_name = "prey_label", weight = "diet_fraction",
                weight_type = "rra",            # relative read abundance, not mass
                unit_label = "scat",            # "scats", not "stomachs", everywhere
                covariates = c("season", "year", "site"))
seal <- dv_prepare(salish_seal_dna, spec, taxonomy = "table",
                   lineage = salish_seal_lineage)
dv_rank_table(dv_tree(seal), "Family")          # pct_w is the mean RRA
dv_resolution(seal, by = "lab")                 # where identification stops

# an ASV table straight from a pipeline
long <- dv_from_wide(asv_table, id_cols = c("asv", "taxonomy"), meta = samples,
                     collapse_by = "taxonomy")
long <- dv_parse_lineage(long, "taxonomy")      # "k__Animalia; p__..." -> rank columns

# terrestrial or freshwater prey
prep <- dv_prepare(dat, spec, taxonomy = "gbif", kingdom = "Animalia")
```

`weight_type = "reads"` gives the pooled share of reads instead.
Biomarker methods such as stable isotopes or fatty acids estimate source
contributions rather than identifying prey, and are out of scope. See
the article [Beyond
stomachs](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/articles/other-data.html).

## Getting help

For bugs or feature requests, please use the [issue
tracker](https://github.com/SostheneA/DietView/issues).

## Citation

``` r

citation("DietView")
```

## Related work

DietView is a visualization and reporting layer; it does not model diet
composition or fit selectivity. It complements diet-analysis workflows
built on `vegan` (multivariate community statistics), to which
[`dv_matrix()`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/dv_matrix.md)
is the direct bridge, the WoRMS toolchain (`worrms`), metabarcoding
pipelines (QIIME 2, DADA2), whose outputs
[`dv_from_wide()`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/dv_from_wide.md)
and
[`dv_parse_lineage()`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/dv_parse_lineage.md)
read, and interactive graphics via `plotly` and `htmlwidgets`. The
sunburst and dashboard design follow the southern Gulf of St. Lawrence
(sGSL) diet dashboard it generalizes.

# Package index

## Package overview

What DietView is and how the pieces fit together.

- [`DietView`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/DietView-package.md)
  [`DietView-package`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/DietView-package.md)
  : DietView: interactive, hierarchical visualization of predator diet
  data

## Example data

Public stomach-content data from the ICES Stomach Content Database
(North Sea, Skagerrak-Kattegat and Baltic Sea, 2020-2024), with their
frozen WoRMS lineage, used throughout the examples and articles; and the
public DNA metabarcoding diet of Salish Sea harbour seals (Thomas et
al. 2022).

- [`ices_diet`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/ices_diet.md)
  : Stomach contents of North-East Atlantic fishes (ICES, 2020-2024)
- [`ices_stomachs`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/ices_stomachs.md)
  : Sampled stomachs of the ICES example data, empty ones included
- [`ices_lineage`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/ices_lineage.md)
  : Frozen WoRMS lineage for the ICES example data
- [`ices_lineage_raw`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/ices_lineage_raw.md)
  : Uncorrected WoRMS lineage for the ICES example data
- [`salish_seal_dna`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/salish_seal_dna.md)
  : DNA metabarcoding diet of Salish Sea harbour seals
- [`salish_seal_lineage`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/salish_seal_lineage.md)
  : Frozen WoRMS lineage for the Salish Sea harbour seal data

## 1 · Declare and validate your data

Describe once how your columns map to DietView’s roles. Nothing is
hard-coded; every other function reads this spec.

- [`dv_spec()`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/dv_spec.md)
  : Declare how your columns map to DietView's roles
- [`dv_validate()`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/dv_validate.md)
  : Check a long diet table against a spec before any work is done

## 1b · Bring other data shapes

Reshape wide sample-by-taxon tables (ASV/OTU tables, catch compositions)
into the long format, and split pipeline lineage strings into rank
columns.

- [`dv_from_wide()`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/dv_from_wide.md)
  : Reshape a wide sample-by-taxon table into DietView's long format
- [`dv_parse_lineage()`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/dv_parse_lineage.md)
  : Split a lineage string into rank columns

## 2 · Attach taxonomy

Resolve prey to the WoRMS classification (marine), the GBIF Backbone
(all kingdoms), or join your own lineage table, keeping unresolved prey
as an explicit unidentified category and logging every match for review.

- [`dv_prepare()`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/dv_prepare.md)
  : Prepare a diet table for DietView (validate + add taxa)
- [`dv_taxonomy_worms()`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/dv_taxonomy_worms.md)
  : Resolve prey to the WoRMS classification (id, exact name, then
  fuzzy)
- [`dv_taxonomy_gbif()`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/dv_taxonomy_gbif.md)
  : Resolve prey to the GBIF Backbone Taxonomy (key, exact name, then
  fuzzy)
- [`dv_taxonomy_report()`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/dv_taxonomy_report.md)
  : Review doubtful prey matches
- [`dv_lineage_check()`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/dv_lineage_check.md)
  : Check a lineage for spelling variants and inconsistent placements
- [`dv_cache_clear()`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/dv_cache_clear.md)
  : Delete the WoRMS and GBIF lookup caches

## 3 · Build covariates

Derive periods and length bins to stratify the views.

- [`dv_add_period()`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/dv_add_period.md)
  : Derive a period covariate from year
- [`dv_size_bins()`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/dv_size_bins.md)
  : Build per-group length bins

## 4 · Compute within-rank importance

Aggregate records into a multi-rank tree where each rank sums to 100
percent, unidentified records included, by prey records (or numbers) and
by weight.

- [`dv_tree()`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/dv_tree.md)
  : Build the diet tree from a prepared dataset, using the columns in
  its spec
- [`dv_build_tree()`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/dv_build_tree.md)
  : Build the multi-rank tree with within-rank importance
- [`dv_rank_table()`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/dv_rank_table.md)
  : Importance table for one rank

## 5 · Draw figures

Render the multi-rank sunburst and its color dictionaries.

- [`dv_sunburst()`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/dv_sunburst.md)
  : Render a diet sunburst
- [`dv_palette()`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/dv_palette.md)
  : Build a color dictionary for taxon labels
- [`dv_palette_tree()`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/dv_palette_tree.md)
  : Colors that follow the taxonomic hierarchy

## 6 · Identification resolution and the digestion bias

The finest rank each record reaches, overall or by any grouping
(predator, method, year), and split by digestion stage.

- [`dv_resolution()`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/dv_resolution.md)
  : Identification resolution: the finest rank each record reaches
- [`dv_digestion_diagnostic()`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/dv_digestion_diagnostic.md)
  : Identification resolution versus digestion level

## 7 · Species identification cards

- [`dv_species_card_assets()`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/dv_species_card_assets.md)
  : Resolve an identification photo and description for a predator

## 8 · Ship a dashboard or explore interactively

A self-contained HTML dashboard, a deploy wrapper, and a Shiny explorer.

- [`dv_build_html()`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/dv_build_html.md)
  : Build a self-contained HTML diet dashboard
- [`dv_deploy()`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/dv_deploy.md)
  : Deploy the dashboard as a standalone HTML file
- [`run_dietview()`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/run_dietview.md)
  : Launch the interactive DietView app
- [`dv_script()`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/dv_script.md)
  : Write a reproducible R script for one DietView analysis

## 9 · Explore, aggregate, and export

Describe the sample, check sampling sufficiency, report classical
frequency of occurrence, aggregate rare prey upward to a reproducible
threshold, and export the sampling-unit by prey-category matrix for
downstream multivariate analysis.

- [`dv_summary()`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/dv_summary.md)
  : Describe the sampled diet dataset
- [`dv_prey_accumulation()`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/dv_prey_accumulation.md)
  : Prey accumulation (cumulative prey) curve for sample sufficiency
- [`dv_fo_table()`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/dv_fo_table.md)
  : Frequency of occurrence per rank (the Buckland Table B1 layout)
- [`dv_aggregate_threshold()`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/dv_aggregate_threshold.md)
  : Aggregate rare prey upward to a stomach-frequency threshold
- [`dv_threshold_sweep()`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/dv_threshold_sweep.md)
  : Count diet categories across a sweep of thresholds
- [`dv_matrix()`](https://sosthenea.github.io/DietView/reference/dv_matrix.md)
  : Build a sampling-unit by prey-category matrix
